transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

This usually happens for one of three reasons: the temperature setting was turned too low (or Fast Freeze left on), food is touching the cold back wall where it freezes instantly, or there’s a defrost fault causing ice to block airflow. To narrow this down quickly:
1. Check if the thermostat dial is set very high/cold or if 'Fast Freeze' was accidentally left on.
2. Check if any items were touching the rear internal wall of the fridge section.
3. If those are fine, we need to check for ice build-up behind the back panel (a defrost issue). Could you tell me: is the temperature dial set very cold or is Fast Freeze active? And were the frozen items touching the back wall?
dial is turned right up to max/coldest, kids prob moved it. and yes the frozen stuff is right against the back wall by the vent slots, fridge is rammed after big shop

That explains it perfectly: setting the dial to 'max' makes the compressor run continuously, which will freeze anything touching the cold back wall. Since your food was right against that wall and the fridge is packed tight, the airflow couldn't circulate properly. Please turn the dial down to a mid-range setting (usually around 3 or 4) immediately. Move all items away from the back wall so air can flow freely between them. Leave it like this for 24 hours with normal use. Has the food thawed out enough to eat, and is the fridge section no longer freezing?
did that, dial to middle and cleared the vents. 2 days on its better but one yoghurt still froze right at the very back. is that normal?

It is not strictly normal for food to freeze at a mid-range setting, but it is very common if airflow isn't perfect. If there is clear space (about 2-3cm) around all items and nothing touches the rear, leave it for another 12 hours. If the rest of the fridge is fine but one item freezes when placed correctly, the thermostat may be slightly over-sensitive; you can try setting the dial one notch warmer to compensate.
ok will try one notch warmer. is it a problem if just one yoghurt at the very back freezes tho, or can i ignore it?
You can safely ignore it. As long as the rest of your food is at a safe temperature and only that single item at the very back freezes when placed correctly, this is not a fault.

candidates: Thermostat setting too cold or Fast Freeze mode left on (high)
Food touching the cold back wall (medium)
Defrost system fault (blocked drain or failed heater) (low)
